title: Introduce traffic-light progressive states and graceful action cancellation for buttons
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Define and consolidate a traffic-light progressive state model for primary and icon buttons (Idle -> Pending -> Outcome), add an explicit in-flight cancel affordance for long-running actions, and stabilize theming/token mappings to prevent regressions across high-contrast and dark themes.
design_decisions: Adopt a three-phase visual model: Idle (neutral), Pending (amber / progress affordance), Outcome (success green OR error red OR cancelled muted).
Pending state will use a compact inline progress indicator plus optional cancel icon button when expected latency > 700ms.
Outcome states should be transient: success shows brief green check for 1.2s before returning to idle or navigating; error shows red outline and full accessible error tooltip.
For icon-only buttons, introduce a focused Halo token rather than changing fill color to avoid layout shift.

Tokens: introduce semantic tokens -- button.pending.bg, button.pending.fg, button.outcome.success.bg, button.outcome.error.border, button.cancel.icon-color. Map them to theme-aware values (light/dark/high-contrast).
Motion reduction: animations should respect prefers-reduced-motion; prefer opacity and transform over layout changes.
Keyboard & screen reader: pending state must expose aria-busy and a live region message; cancel must be keyboard-focusable and announceable.
Graceful rollback: when server responds with change-of-state, UI must animate to outcome but keep action idempotent until user sees success notification.
engineering_notes: Frontend: Add button variants 'progressive' modifier and CSS variables for new semantic tokens. Implement cancel affordance as separate interactive element inside the button container to preserve hit target.

API contract: recommend response schema include {status: 'pending'|'success'|'error'|'cancelled', message?: string, suggestedClientAction?: 'noop'|'retry'|'rollback'}. Backcompat: default to 'success' on missing field.
Performance: pending heuristics should only enable cancel affordance after 700ms to avoid UI noise for fast requests.
Testing: include e2e tests that simulate slow server and assert cancel triggers a client-side abort + telemetry event.
Telemetry: emit events 'btn.pending_shown', 'btn.cancel_clicked', 'btn.outcome_received' with action id. Ensure telemetry keys documented in ops playbook.
CSS: use --rdw-button-pending-bg, --rdw-button-pending-fg, --rdw-button-outcome-success-bg, --rdw-button-outcome-error-border tokens. Map these to theme tokens in runtime token mapper.
acceptance_criteria: Primary and secondary buttons support new 'progressive' state with visual Pending + Outcome transitions.
Cancel affordance appears only after 700ms for long-running actions and is keyboard accessible and screen reader announced.
No layout shift occurs when toggling states for both text and icon-only buttons.
All tokens resolve correctly in light, dark and high-contrast themes without contrast regression (WCAG AA for normal text).
QA regression suite: existing button stories must pass. Add three new Storybook stories: Primary progressive, Icon-only progressive, Cancel flow.
E2E test covers: show pending, click cancel, verify abort + 'btn.cancel_clicked' telemetry emitted.
Design review sign-off recorded in Confluence and Figma links are attached to the ticket.
qa_checks: Verify aria-busy on button during pending and announced live region messages.
Tab order includes cancel control and it supports Enter/Space to cancel.
Color-checks: pending amber against background >= 4.5:1 for readability of progress icon label; outcome green used only for transient check icon not for main CTA color to avoid mixed affordances.
Reduced-motion: ensure no parallax/large transforms when prefers-reduced-motion is set.
Regression checklist: run visual diff across 6 primary button stories in default themes and dark/high-contrast.
